title: GND transition steps document
description: A WALK: the ordered operation invocations that are claimed to have carried a population from a pre-state to a post-state. Layer 1 only -- shape. Whether an `op` names a declared operation, whether `bindings` supply exactly that operation's parameters, and whether every digest matches are layer-2 questions answered by gnd.transition, which reports them as transition:* rule ids. The normative account of what each field means and why three digests are computed three different ways lives in representation-format.md; this file constrains bytes, not meaning.

steps_schema.description: Format version. One value today; a second would be a format change with its own migration.

model.description: The model this walk was authored against, for a human reader. DELIBERATELY INERT: it is never opened, never resolved to a path, and never compared to the MODEL argument of the command. A field that selected a model would be a second, unauthenticated way to choose one, and the CLI argument is the only way.

model_digest.description: sha256 of the loaded model object, as population._model_digest computes it. It deliberately EXCLUDES the operations section, which is exactly why operations_digest exists.

operations_digest.description: sha256 over canonical JSON of the raw operations section, as loaded and BEFORE compilation attaches anything. `[]` for a v1 document and for an absent or empty section, so those three share one value. Printed by `gnd validate MODEL --trace`, which is its shipped producer.

pre_digest.description: OPTIONAL provenance pin: sha256 over the pre-population FILE BYTES as read. Present means it must match; absent is structurally fine. Bytes rather than content, because the question is whether this is the artifact the walk was written against.

steps.description: The walk, in order. Step identity is the 1-based index into this array. At least one step: a transition run over zero steps is a snapshot check wearing a costume, and the snapshot arm already exists.

op.description: The id of a declared operation. That it names one is layer 2's question (transition:unknown-operation).

bindings.description: A value for every declared parameter of the operation, and no others -- layer 2 checks that (transition:bindings-mismatch), and checks each value against its parameter's object type (transition:binding-type). Scalars only: a walk binds values, never structures.
